newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker as market corrects.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker as market corrects.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker as the market corrected following recent gains and a failure to maintain upside momentum amid losses across the base metals board, dealers said.

But market watchers were keeping a close watch on the vote at Inco's Sudbury nickel and copper plant Monday, with rumors that rank and file members opposed the tentative deal agreed Friday by their leaders and the company.
July COMEX copper settled 1.95 cents per pound weaker at 117.15 cents a pound, traded 117.20 to 115.90 cents. Spot June was off 1.60 cents at 117.00 cents. Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots.

"There was some consumer hedge buying far forward, and lower prices have led to reduced producer selling. The other featured sellers were the funds," Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said. "A lot of this was spillover selling from the other base metals."
LME stocks fell a nominal 200 tonnes to 133,025 tonnes Monday.

Copper has been moving sideways in overbought territory for over a week and a correction of some sort was inevitable, dealers said. But low inventories may help the market retest the recent highs, they added.
